notes: Annual report of the Playground Commission for 1911-12. Curated: the Excelsior, Hamilton, Holly Park, Presidio Heights, Spring Valley and Mission sites, Jackson Playground's dedication, the North Beach swimming tank.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: Southside Playground at Seventh and Harrison (later Father Crowley; no page); the 1898 California Club playground at Bush and Hyde (no page); a playground beside the Lick Baths on Tenth Street. The 1925-26 report in the same item is a directory of playgrounds; its opening months are ambiguous in the OCR and were not used.

findings.description: Answering petitions from Excelsior Homestead residents, the Board of Supervisors bought the two-acre site bounded by Persia, Russia, Madrid and Edinburgh Streets for the Playground Commission in July for $21,000; building the playground waited for 1912-13 funds.

findings.description: Jackson Playground, on land the Park Commission had deeded to the Playground Commission in July 1909, was dedicated by Mayor James Rolph Jr. on Labor Day, September 2, with a Municipal Band concert and football, basketball and handball games.

findings.description: The city's first free swimming tank, a 50 by 90 foot salt-water plunge of reinforced concrete, was built on North Beach Playground for $6,817.13 in the fiscal year ending that June. A concrete bathhouse around it in the Mission style, with dressing rooms, the playground's offices and a red tile roof, designed by the Bureau of Architecture of the Board of Public Works, was then funded with $12,704 and expected to open the following January.
